# Adjudication Task — Chapter 184

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃184화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|수백이 아니라 천 명도 될 것 같다. 우리는 태원진가 무인들의 경호를 받으며 엄청나게 몰려든 인파 속을 헤쳐 나갔다.
  6|
  7|‘기분 끝내주네.’
  8|
  9|중화권 스타가 된 기분이다. 한류 열풍 뭐 그런 거.
 10|
 11|아니, 실제로 한국인이니까 틀린 말은 아닌가?
 12|
 13|“산서잠룡! 여기 한 번만 봐 주시오!”
 14|
 15|“꺄악! 진 소협!”
 16|
 17|“응애애애!”
 18|
 19|똥개도 자기 집에서는 반은 먹고 들어간다고 했다.
 20|
 21|아무리 매화삼절이 유명해도 산서성의 자랑, 태원의 아들을 홈그라운드에서 이길 수는 없었다.
 22|
 23|흐뭇하게 웃으며 손을 흔드는 내게 철우가 속삭였다.
 24|
 25|“입꼬리 올라간 것 봐라. 좋냐?”
 26|
 27|“입꼬리 내려간 것 봐라. 우냐?”
 28|
 29|“이 산서성 촌놈이.”
 30|
 31|“네, 다음 자연인.”
 32|
 33|“이런 개…….”
 34|
 35|“뭐, 이…….”
 36|
 37|다시 한번 불꽃이 튀려던 그때, 한 줄기 전음이 귓가를 파고들었다.
 38|
 39|- 삼공자!
 40|
 41|위팽이 험악한 표정으로 나를 노려보는 중이었다. 당장 뺨이라도 한 대 갈기고 싶어 하는 얼굴이다.
 42|
 43|철우에게도 비슷한 전음을 보냈는지 놈도 불만 섞인 얼굴로 한마디를 툭 덧붙였다.
 44|
 45|“봐줬다.”
 46|
 47|나는 코웃음으로 대답을 대신했다.
 48|
 49|사람들의 환호성을 듣고 철우, 저놈이 화산파에서도 제법 잘 나가는 후기지수라는 걸 처음 알았을 때는 꽤 놀랐지만 그뿐이었다.
 50|
 51|‘매화삼절이면 뭐, 어쩌라고?’
 52|
 53|화산파의 무공이라면 이미 충분히 겪어 봤다. 내 옆에서 털레털레 걷고 있는 어떤 한 사람 덕분에.
 54|
 55|“배고파. 배고파요.”
 56|
 57|“…….”
 58|
 59|언제 봐도 희한한 놈이지만 청풍이 화산파의 진산절학을 섭렵한 절정 고수라는 건 부정할 수 없는 사실이다.
 60|
 61|때문에 철우가 어떤 무공을 사용하더라도 대응할 자신이 있었다. 놈이 나보다 앞서는 거라고는 화산파라는 배경뿐이다.
 62|
 63|“…….”
 64|
 65|아, 아니다. 방금 했던 말 취소.
 66|
 67|다시 생각해 보니까 배경 차이가 심각하다. 태원진가의 위상이 아무리 올랐어도 구파일방은 압도적이다.
 68|
 69|‘시벌, 졌네.’
 70|
 71|내가 생각하는 구파일방, 천하오대세가는 무림의 기업 연합이나 다름없다. 안 그래도 힘센 대기업들이 연합체를 꾸려서 다구리를 놓으니 당할 놈들이 없는 거다.
 72|
 73|다행히 나름 정파랍시고 골목 상권까지 침범하진 않아서 태원진가 같은 중소기업도 위로 치고 올라가는 거지.
 74|
 75|‘그런 의미에서 화산파가 이 일에 신경을 많이 쓰고 있는 건 확실하고.’
 76|
 77|화산일학 백무성.
 78|
 79|혁무진이 떠들어 댄 것들이 사실이라면 그는 자타가 인정하는 화산파 차기 장문인이나 다름없다.
 80|
 81|그나마 화산파의 후기지수 중 그에 견줄 만한 유일한 상대가 있긴 한데…….
 82|
 83|“은인, 저 진짜 배고파요. 혹시 만두 남은 거 없어요?”
 84|
 85|“네. 없는데요.”
 86|
 87|“앗. 아아아…….”
 88|
 89|청풍은 안 될 거야, 아마.
 90|
 91|저 인간이 화산파 장문인이 되는 것보다 화산파 도사들이 이슬람교로 개종하는 게 더 빠를 거다.
 92|
 93|제삼자인 내 눈에도 뭐 이런 놈이 있나 싶은데 화산파 사람들이 보면 오죽할까.
 94|
 95|‘나중에 세상의 모든 일을 경험하고 나면, 그때가 돼서야 화산파 장문인도 해 보고 싶다고 할 놈이지. 음.’
 96|
 97|내가 상당히 신빙성 있는 미래를 상상하고 있을 때, 철우가 짜증 난 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
 98|
 99|“거, 만두 못 먹어서 죽은 귀신이라도 붙었소? 제발 입 좀 다물고 갑시다.”
100|
101|“……?”
102|
103|“……?”
104|
105|“……?”
106|
107|순간 나와 위팽, 혁무진의 시선을 한 몸에 받은 철우가 흠칫 놀랐다.
108|
109|“뭐, 뭔데? 갑자기 왜 그런 눈으로 쳐다보는 거요?”
110|
111|“야, 너 혹시.”
112|
113|“철 소협, 모르시오?”
114|
115|“에이, 설마요. 명색이 매화삼절이신데 그걸 모르실 리가.”
116|
117|줄줄이 이어지는 반응에 철우가 황소 같은 눈을 뒤룩뒤룩 굴렸다.
118|
119|“뭐야? 왜 이러는 건데?”
120|
121|왜 이러긴, 사문의 어르신도 못 알아보니 이러지.
122|
123|항렬로 따졌을 때, 청풍은 검성의 제자이자 현 화산파 장문인인 천검진인의 막내 사제가 된다.
124|
125|철우에게는 스승님의 사제, 즉 사숙(師叔)인 셈이다.
126|
127|‘아, 생각해 보니 모를 수도 있겠네.’
128|
129|청풍은 검성 매종학이 은거 중에 키운 제자다. 문파 내부에서도 극소수만이 그의 얼굴과 정체를 알고 있을 게 분명했다.
130|
131|나는 사숙을 눈앞에 두고도 못 알아보는 철우를 보며 혀를 찼다.
132|
133|“쯧쯧. 등잔 밑이 어둡다더니.”
134|
135|“그러니까 그게 무슨 소리냐고.”
136|
137|“아냐, 잠시 후면 알게 되겠지.”
138|
139|“이런 니기미, 환장하겠네.”
140|
141|철우가 답답함에 가슴을 칠 때, 우리는 군중들의 환호를 뒤로하고 태원진가의 정문으로 들어섰다.
142|
143|동시에 사방에서 백여 쌍의 시선과 수군거림이 날아들었다. 문밖과는 사뭇 다른 분위기다.
144|
145|“저 청년이…….”
146|
147|“산서잠룡이군요. 듣던 대로 영준합니다.”
148|
149|“패화권도 있군. 천검진인의 둘째 제자라지?”
150|
151|“그런데 옆에 있는 두 청년은 누굽니까?”
152|
153|“글쎄올시다.”
154|
155|남녀노소의 구분 없이 섞여 있는 백여 명의 사람들. 옷차림과 태도에서 그들이 가진 부와 여유가 묻어 나온다.
156|
157|‘산서성의 실력자들.’
158|
159|그들 중에는 일문(一門)의 문주들도 있고, 상계(商界)의 부호들도 있다. 이번 회합에 정식으로 초청받을 만큼의 세력과 능력이 있는 자들이었다.
160|
161|‘얼핏 보면 귀족들의 무도회 같기도 하고.’
162|
163|나는 묘한 기분에 휩싸여 걸음을 옮겼다.
164|
165|산서성의 지배층이라 할 수 있는 저들이 이 회합의 조연에 불과하다는 사실에, 그리고 저들이 보내는 호기심과 선망 어린 시선에 마음 한구석이 간질거렸다.
166|
167|그리고 다음 순간이었다.
168|
169|“하곡문(河曲門)이라는 자그마한 문파를 이끌고 있는 장세팔이라고 하오.”
170|
171|“아, 네. 안녕하세요.”
172|
173|“다름이 아니라, 평소 태원진가와 산서잠룡의 명성을 마음 깊이 흠모하고 있었는데…….”
174|
175|이렇게 만나게 되어 영광이라는 말을 장황하게 늘어놓는 중년 무인을 시작으로 사람들이 좀비 떼처럼 몰려들기 시작했다.
176|
177|“안녕하십니까. 소인은 양천 근처에서 작은 무관을 운영 중인…….”
178|
179|“예? 아, 예.”
180|
181|“진 소협. 내 긴히 할 말이 있는데 자리를 옮기는 것이…….”
182|
183|“지금이요? 그건 좀.”
184|
185|“이 아이는 내 여식이오. 산서잠룡을 꼭 한번 보고 싶다기에 데려왔는데 혹시 마음에 든다면…….”
186|
187|“예, 예.”
188|
189|“오오, 그럼 바로 매파를 보내면 되겠소?”
190|
191|“잠깐, 잠깐만요! 잘못 대답했어요!”
192|
193|이게 도대체 무슨 일이래.
194|
195|사방에서 쏟아지는 악수의 요청, 아니 포권 세례에 혼이 쏙 빠질 지경이다.
196|
197|때마침 위팽이 나서지 않았다면 온갖 미사여구가 들어간 청탁과 혼례 요청을 죄다 수락해야 했을 것이다.
198|
199|“모두 자중하시오!”
200|
201|공력이 실린 절정 고수의 외침에 사람들이 움찔한 틈을 타 자리를 빠져나왔다. 철우가 질렸다는 듯이 혀를 내두른다.
202|
203|“극성이군. 산서성 사람들은 죄다 저런가?”
204|
205|그럴 리가 있냐. 이번 경우가 좀 특수한 거지.
206|
207|일행 중 당황하지 않은 사람은 위팽뿐이었다. 그가 덤덤한 표정으로 입을 열었다.
208|
209|“앞으로 자주 겪을 일이니 차차 익숙해져야 할 겁니다.”
210|
211|“오늘 같은 일을 자주 겪어야 한다고요?”
212|
213|“삼공자는 태원진가의 직계니까요.”
214|
215|“방금 혼인만 다섯 번 치를 뻔했어요.”
216|
217|“반려자가 없는 전도유망한 후기지수에게는 당연한 일이죠.”
218|
219|“아까 들어 보니 저랑 태중 혼약을 맺었다는 사람도 있던데…… 그거 사실입니까?”
220|
221|“사실이면 어떻고 거짓이면 어떻습니까? 좋게 생각하십시오.”
222|
223|머리털이 쭈뼛 선다. 현실에서 27년간 모태 솔로로 살았는데 난데없이 중매로 결혼하는 게 아닌가 싶어서다.
224|
225|그것도 만리타향인 무림에서.
226|
227|‘안 돼. 나한테는 송이 씨가 있어.’
228|
229|나는 목에 핏대까지 세우며 외쳤다.
230|
231|“아니, 혼인이 얼마나 중요한 일인데 그걸 그렇게 넘어가면 안 되죠! 남녀 간의 사랑! 순수한 감정! 저한테는 그런 것도 없어요?”
232|
233|“예. 없습니다.”
234|
235|“왜! 어째서!”
236|
237|위팽이 벌레를 보는 듯한 눈빛으로 나를 훑었다.
238|
239|“그게 열여섯 살 때부터 기루에 들락거린 사람이 할 소립니까? 은자 뿌리면서 양심도 같이 뿌렸어요?”
240|
241|“…….”
242|
243|“조용히 갑시다. 주군께서 기다리고 계십니다.”
244|
245|차라리 가 봤으면 억울하지나 않지.
246|
247|기루는 시발, 헌팅 술집도 못 가 봤는데.
248|
249|말도 못 하고 내심 피눈물만 흘리는 내게 철우가 슬쩍 물었다.
250|
251|“사실이냐?”
252|
253|“뭐가.”
254|
255|“열여섯 살 때부터 기루 간 거.”
256|
257|“알 거 없어. 그리고 갑자기 그딴 건 왜 물어봐?”
258|
259|순간 흠칫한 철우가 횡설수설했다.
260|
261|“그, 뭐랄까. 개인적인 호기심이랄까. 우직하게 무인의 길만을 걸어온 한 사내의…….”
262|
263|“기루에 가 보고 싶다고?”
264|
265|“커흐흠!”
266|
267|“……무인의 길이나 마저 걸어라. 괜히 샛길로 빠지지 말고.”
268|
269|한심한 감정을 가득 담아 대답한 그때였다.
270|
271|“진 소협의 말씀이 백번 옳다. 본산에서 내려온 지 얼마나 되었다고 벌써부터 무인의 본분을 잊은 것이냐?”
272|
273|엄하면서도 웃음기가 담긴 말투.
274|
275|낯선 목소리의 주인공은 말끔한 인상의 사내였다. 흔들림 없는 걸음으로 다가온 그가 공손히 포권을 취했다.
276|
277|그 대상은 나도, 위팽도 아니었다.
278|
279|“화산파 일대제자 백무성이 사숙을 뵙습니다.”
280|
281|잠깐 침묵하던 청풍이 대답했다.
282|
283|“누구세요?”
284|
285|
286|
287|* * *
288|
289|
290|
291|환갑쯤 되었을까?
292|
293|호리호리한 키에 쭉 째진 눈매가 인상적인 노인이었다.
294|
295|거스러미가 돋아난 입술 사이에서는 잔뜩 쉰 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
296|
297|“그래서 이름도 없는 무명 소졸에게 개망신을 당했다?”
298|
299|“자, 장로님. 그것이 아니오라…….”
300|
301|노인의 앞에 선 세 명의 사내는 땀을 뻘뻘 흘렸다.
302|
303|종남삼수(終南三手)라 불리는 그들이지만 사문의 존장 앞에서는 말 한마디, 행동거지 하나하나에 주의를 기울여야 한다.
304|
305|그 상대가 종남파에서 다섯 손가락 안에 꼽히는 고수이자 불같은 성격으로 유명한 노호검객(怒號劍客)이라면 더더욱.
306|
307|“그럼 무엇이냐? 아무리 들어도 노부의 귀에는 네놈들이 대 종남파의 이름에 똥칠했다는 소리로 들리는데.”
308|
309|날카로운 눈빛에 종남삼수가 몸을 부르르 떨었다.
310|

Cheongpung was a strange guy no matter how many times I saw him, but there was no denying that he was a Peak master who had mastered Huashan’s supreme secret arts.

[P31]
Thanks to him, I was confident I could counter whatever martial arts Chulwoo used. The only thing Chulwoo had over me was Huashan’s backing.

[P32]
“……”

[P33]
Ah, no. I take that back.

[P34]
Now that I thought about it, the difference in our backgrounds was pretty serious. No matter how far the Jin Family of Taiyuan had risen, the Nine Sects and One Gang were overwhelmingly powerful.

[P35]
*Fuck. I lose.*

[P36]
The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were essentially Murim’s version of a corporate alliance.

[P37]
A bunch of already powerful conglomerates had banded together to gang up on everyone else. Who could possibly stand against that?

[P38]
Fortunately, for all their talk of being the orthodox faction, they didn’t encroach on the neighborhood markets. That was why small and medium-sized companies like the Jin Family of Taiyuan still had room to climb.

[P39]
*Seen that way, Huashan is clearly paying close attention to this matter.*

[P40]
Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong.

[P41]
If everything Hyuk Mujin had told me was true, Baek Museong was all but universally acknowledged as Huashan’s next Sect Leader.

[P42]
There was one person among Huashan’s young prodigies who could rival him, though…

[P43]
“Benefactor, I’m really hungry. Do you have any dumplings left?”

[P44]
“No. I don’t.”

[P45]
“Oh. Aaaah…”

[P46]
Cheongpung was a lost cause.

[P47]
Huashan’s Daoists would probably convert to Islam before that guy became the Sect Leader of Huashan.

[P48]

[P49]
*He’s the kind of guy who’ll experience everything the world has to offer, then decide he’d like to try being Huashan’s Sect Leader too. Yeah.*

[P51]
“What, are you possessed by the ghost of someone who died craving dumplings? Please shut up and walk.”

[P52]
“……?”

[P53]
“……?”

[P54]
“……?”

[P55]
Chulwoo flinched as Wipeng, Hyuk Mujin, and I all turned to stare at him.

[P56]
“W-What? Why are you suddenly looking at me like that?”

[P57]
“Hey, don’t tell me…”

[P58]
“Young Hero Chul, you don’t know?”

[P59]
“Come on, surely not. You’re one of the Three Plum Blossom Elites. There’s no way you wouldn’t know.”

[P60]
As our reactions came one after another, Chulwoo’s ox-like eyes darted around.

[P61]
“What? Why is everyone acting like this?”

[P62]
Why else? Because he couldn’t recognize an elder of his own sect.

[P63]
In terms of seniority, Cheongpung was the Sword Saint’s Disciple and the youngest Junior Brother of the Heavenly Sword True Person, Huashan’s current Sect Leader.

[P64]
That made him Chulwoo’s master’s Junior Brother—in other words, his Martial Uncle.

[P65]
*Actually, now that I think about it, maybe he wouldn’t know.*

[P66]
The Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak, had raised Cheongpung while living in seclusion. Only a select few within Huashan could possibly know his face and identity.

[P67]
I clicked my tongue at Chulwoo, who was standing right in front of his Martial Uncle without recognizing him.

[P68]
“Tsk, tsk. It really is darkest beneath the lamp.”

[P69]
“What the hell are you talking about?”

[P70]
“Never mind. You’ll find out soon enough.”

[P71]
“Damn it, this is driving me insane.”

[P72]
As Chulwoo pounded his chest in frustration, we left the cheering crowd behind and passed through the main gate of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P73]

[P74]
“That young man…”

[P75]
“That’s the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. He’s every bit as handsome as I’d heard.”

[P76]
“The Defeated Flower Fist is here too. Isn’t he the Heavenly Sword True Person’s second Disciple?”

[P77]
“Then who are the two young men beside them?”

[P78]
“I couldn’t tell you.”

[P79]

[P80]
*The power players of Shanxi Province.*

[P82]
*At first glance, it almost looks like an aristocratic ball.*

[P83]

[P84]

[P85]

[P86]
“My name is Jang Se-pal. I lead a small sect called the Hequ Sect.”

[P87]
“Ah, yes. Hello.”

[P88]
“I have long admired the reputation of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, and…”

[P89]

[P90]
“Greetings. I run a small martial arts academy near Yangcheon…”

[P91]
“Pardon? Oh, yes.”

[P92]
“Young Hero Jin, I have something important to discuss with you. Perhaps we could speak somewhere more private…”

[P93]
“Right now? That might be difficult.”

[P94]
“This is my daughter. She insisted on seeing the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi at least once, so I brought her with me. If she happens to appeal to you…”

[P95]
“Yes, yes.”

[P96]
“Oh! Then shall I send a matchmaker at once?”

[P97]
“Wait, wait! I answered that wrong!”

[P98]
What the hell was going on?

[P99]
Requests for handshakes—or rather, a barrage of fist-and-palm salutes—poured in from every direction. I was on the verge of losing my mind.

[P100]
If Wipeng hadn’t stepped forward at just the right moment, I might have agreed to every favor and marriage proposal buried beneath all that flowery praise.

[P101]
“Everyone, restrain yourselves!”

[P102]

[P103]
“That was excessive. Are all the people of Shanxi like that?”

[P104]
Of course not. This was a special case.

[P105]

[P106]
“This will happen often from now on, so you should gradually get used to it.”

[P107]
“I’m going to experience things like this often?”

[P108]
“You’re a direct descendant of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P109]
“I almost got married five times just now.”

[P110]
“That’s only natural for a promising young prodigy without a partner.”

[P111]
“I heard someone claim they were betrothed to me while we were still in the womb… Is that true?”

[P112]
“What does it matter whether it’s true or false? Look on the bright side.”

[P113]
My hair stood on end.

[P114]
I’d spent twenty-seven years in the modern world without ever dating anyone, and now I was afraid I might suddenly end up in an arranged marriage.

[P115]
In Murim, thousands of miles from home, no less.

[P116]
*No. I have Song-i.*

[P117]
Veins bulging in my neck, I shouted,

[P118]
“Marriage is incredibly important! You can’t just brush it aside like that! Love between a man and a woman! Pure feelings! Don’t I get any of that?”

[P119]
“No. You don’t.”

[P120]
“Why?! Why not?!”

[P121]
Wipeng looked me up and down as if I were an insect.

[P122]
“Is that something a man who’s been frequenting pleasure houses since he was sixteen should say? Did you scatter your conscience along with your silver nyang?”

[P123]
“……”

[P124]
“Let’s keep moving quietly. Our Lord is waiting.”

[P125]
If I’d actually been to one, at least I wouldn’t have felt so wronged.

[P126]
Fuck pleasure houses. I’d never even been to a pickup bar.

[P127]
As I kept silent and wept tears of blood inside, Chulwoo sidled over and asked,

[P128]
“Is that true?”

[P129]
“What is?”

[P130]
“That you’ve been visiting pleasure houses since you were sixteen.”

[P131]
“None of your business. Why are you suddenly asking?”

[P132]
Chulwoo flinched and began to ramble.

[P133]
“Well, how should I put it? Personal curiosity, perhaps. The curiosity of a man who has steadfastly walked only the path of a martial artist…”

[P134]
“You want to visit a pleasure house?”

[P135]
“Ahem!”

[P136]
“Stick to the path of a martial artist. Don’t wander down side roads.”

[P137]
I had barely finished answering with utter disdain when a voice cut in.

[P138]
“Young Hero Jin is absolutely right. How long has it been since you descended from the main sect? Have you already forgotten the duty of a martial artist?”

[P139]
The tone was stern, yet tinged with amusement.

[P140]
The unfamiliar voice belonged to a clean-cut man. He approached with steady steps and respectfully offered a fist-and-palm salute.

[P141]
But it wasn’t directed at me or Wipeng.

[P142]
“Baek Museong, First-generation Disciple of Huashan, pays his respects to his Martial Uncle.”

[P143]
Cheongpung remained silent for a moment before answering.

[P144]
“Who are you?”

[P145]
* * *

[P146]
He looked to be around sixty.

[P147]
The old man had a slender frame and strikingly narrow eyes.

[P148]
A deeply hoarse voice rasped through his chapped lips.

[P149]
“So you were utterly humiliated by some nameless nobody?”

[P150]
“E-Elder, that isn’t what happened…”

[P151]
The three men standing before him were sweating profusely.

[P152]
They were known as the Three Hands of Zhongnan, but in the presence of an elder of their sect, they had to watch every word and every movement.

[P153]
All the more so when that elder was the Roaring Fury Swordsman, a master counted among the five strongest in the Zhongnan Sect and a man notorious for his fiery temper.

[P154]
“Then what happened? No matter how I listen to this, all these old ears hear is that you bastards smeared shit all over the name of the great Zhongnan Sect.”

[P155]
The Three Hands of Zhongnan trembled beneath his piercing gaze.

[P156]
Just as the Roaring Fury Swordsman was about to unleash his wrath, one of the men, who had kept his mouth tightly shut the entire time, suddenly spoke.

[P157]
“He wasn’t a nameless nobody.”

[P158]
“What?”

[P159]
Gong Ilhyuk, the man with a splint on his arm, continued.

[P160]
“He said he was the Sword Saint’s Disciple.”

[P161]
The revelation was so shocking that the Roaring Fury Swordsman fell speechless. After a moment, he asked in disbelief,

[P162]
“…The Sword Saint?”

[P163]
“Yes.”

[P164]
“The Sword Saint, who has lived in seclusion all these years, raised a Disciple?”

[P165]
“We doubted him at first, but… it seems to be true.”

[P166]
“Your evidence?”

[P167]
“Li Feng, a lay Disciple of Huashan, serves in the military of Shanxi Province. Judging by his reaction, there can be little doubt.”

[P168]
“Li Feng?”

[P169]
The old man’s already wrinkled brow furrowed further.

[P170]
His memory wasn’t sharp enough to recall some lay Disciple of Huashan.

[P171]
“Is that all?”

[P172]
At the lukewarm response, Gong Ilhyuk hurriedly continued.

[P173]
“He has mastered Huashan’s supreme secret arts to the Peak level despite being barely twenty. He displayed one martial art after another that only the main sect’s direct Disciples are permitted to learn…”

[P174]
After hearing the full account of what had happened, the Roaring Fury Swordsman silently stroked his sword scabbard.

[P175]
*The Sword Saint’s Disciple. The Sword Saint’s Disciple.*

[P176]
The Sword Saint had been in seclusion for decades.

[P177]
No one even knew whether he was alive or dead, yet now his Disciple had suddenly appeared in Murim?

[P178]
It was hard to believe, but the Roaring Fury Swordsman was already inclined to accept it.

[P179]
*At the very least, I should confirm it for myself.*

[P180]
After a long silence, the Roaring Fury Swordsman abruptly rose from his seat and issued an order to the startled Three Hands of Zhongnan.

[P181]
“Guide me.”

[P182]
“W-Where?”

[P183]
“Do you mean to the Sword Saint’s Disciple…?”

[P184]
Unlike the other two, who stood there flustered, Gong Ilhyuk’s eyes flashed.

[P185]
“As far as I know, he is traveling with a scion of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P186]
“A scion of the Jin Family of Taiyuan? You mean that Jin Taekyung fellow you mentioned earlier?”

[P187]
“Yes. He’s half a day’s journey from here.”

[P188]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman clicked his tongue.

[P189]
“You cunning bastard. That’s why you came looking for this old man, isn’t it?”

[P190]
“The name of the great Zhongnan Sect has been dragged through the dirt because of your inept Disciples. Elder, no one cares more deeply for our sect than you. I happened to hear that you were nearby on business, so…”

[P191]
“Enough. From what you’ve told me, that Jin Taekyung fellow sounds extraordinarily arrogant as well.”

[P192]
“That’s right. A bastard like him needs to be taught a harsh lesson.”

[P193]
As if the thought had only just occurred to him, Gong Ilhyuk added,

[P194]
“I hear the Jin Family of Taiyuan is holding a gathering.”

[P195]
“A gathering?”

[P196]
“They invited every sect in Shanxi Province so they could flaunt their power.”

[P197]
“They trampled on our sect, and now they’re holding a gathering?”

[P198]
Anger flared in the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes.

[P199]
“I’ve heard enough. Lead the way.”

[P200]
“I obey, Elder.”

[P201]
A triumphant smile spread across Gong Ilhyuk’s lips.

- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 184

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃184화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|수백이 아니라 천 명도 될 것 같다. 우리는 태원진가 무인들의 경호를 받으며 엄청나게 몰려든 인파 속을 헤쳐 나갔다.
  6|
  7|‘기분 끝내주네.’
  8|
  9|중화권 스타가 된 기분이다. 한류 열풍 뭐 그런 거.
 10|
 11|아니, 실제로 한국인이니까 틀린 말은 아닌가?
 12|
 13|“산서잠룡! 여기 한 번만 봐 주시오!”
 14|
 15|“꺄악! 진 소협!”
 16|
 17|“응애애애!”
 18|
 19|똥개도 자기 집에서는 반은 먹고 들어간다고 했다.
 20|
 21|아무리 매화삼절이 유명해도 산서성의 자랑, 태원의 아들을 홈그라운드에서 이길 수는 없었다.
 22|
 23|흐뭇하게 웃으며 손을 흔드는 내게 철우가 속삭였다.
 24|
 25|“입꼬리 올라간 것 봐라. 좋냐?”
 26|
 27|“입꼬리 내려간 것 봐라. 우냐?”
 28|
 29|“이 산서성 촌놈이.”
 30|
 31|“네, 다음 자연인.”
 32|
 33|“이런 개…….”
 34|
 35|“뭐, 이…….”
 36|
 37|다시 한번 불꽃이 튀려던 그때, 한 줄기 전음이 귓가를 파고들었다.
 38|
 39|- 삼공자!
 40|
 41|위팽이 험악한 표정으로 나를 노려보는 중이었다. 당장 뺨이라도 한 대 갈기고 싶어 하는 얼굴이다.
 42|
 43|철우에게도 비슷한 전음을 보냈는지 놈도 불만 섞인 얼굴로 한마디를 툭 덧붙였다.
 44|
 45|“봐줬다.”
 46|
 47|나는 코웃음으로 대답을 대신했다.
 48|
 49|사람들의 환호성을 듣고 철우, 저놈이 화산파에서도 제법 잘 나가는 후기지수라는 걸 처음 알았을 때는 꽤 놀랐지만 그뿐이었다.
 50|
 51|‘매화삼절이면 뭐, 어쩌라고?’
 52|
 53|화산파의 무공이라면 이미 충분히 겪어 봤다. 내 옆에서 털레털레 걷고 있는 어떤 한 사람 덕분에.
 54|
 55|“배고파. 배고파요.”
 56|
 57|“…….”
 58|
 59|언제 봐도 희한한 놈이지만 청풍이 화산파의 진산절학을 섭렵한 절정 고수라는 건 부정할 수 없는 사실이다.
 60|
 61|때문에 철우가 어떤 무공을 사용하더라도 대응할 자신이 있었다. 놈이 나보다 앞서는 거라고는 화산파라는 배경뿐이다.
 62|
 63|“…….”
 64|
 65|아, 아니다. 방금 했던 말 취소.
 66|

[P85]
Then it happened.

[P86]
“My name is Jang Se-pal. I lead a small sect called the Hequ Sect.”

[P87]
“Ah, yes. Hello.”

[P88]
“I have long admired the reputation of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, and…”

[P89]

[P90]
“Greetings. I run a small martial arts academy near Yangcheon…”

[P91]
“Pardon? Oh, yes.”

[P92]
“Young Hero Jin, I have something important to discuss with you. Perhaps we could speak somewhere more private…”

[P93]
“Right now? That might be difficult.”

[P94]
“This is my daughter. She insisted on seeing the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi at least once, so I brought her with me. If she happens to appeal to you…”

[P95]
“Yes, yes.”

[P96]
“Oh! Then shall I send a matchmaker at once?”

[P97]
“Wait, wait! I answered that wrong!”

[P98]
What the hell was going on?

[P99]
Requests for handshakes—or rather, a barrage of fist-and-palm salutes—poured in from every direction. I was on the verge of losing my mind.

[P100]
If Wipeng hadn’t stepped forward at just the right moment, I might have agreed to every favor and marriage proposal buried beneath all that flowery praise.

[P101]
“Everyone, restrain yourselves!”

[P102]
The shout of a Peak master, infused with internal energy, made the crowd flinch. We seized the opportunity to escape. Chulwoo shook his head in disgust.

[P103]
“That was excessive. Are all the people of Shanxi like that?”

[P104]
Of course not. This was a special case.

[P105]
Wipeng was the only member of our group who hadn’t been flustered. He spoke with his usual calm expression.

[P106]
“This will happen often from now on, so you should gradually get used to it.”

[P107]
“I’m going to experience things like this often?”

[P108]
“You’re a direct descendant of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P109]
“I almost got married five times just now.”

[P110]
“That’s only natural for a promising young prodigy without a partner.”

[P111]
“I heard someone claim they were betrothed to me while we were still in the womb… Is that true?”

[P112]
“What does it matter whether it’s true or false? Look on the bright side.”

[P113]
My hair stood on end.

[P114]
I’d spent twenty-seven years in the modern world without ever dating anyone, and now I was afraid I might suddenly end up in an arranged marriage.

[P115]
In Murim, thousands of miles from home, no less.

[P116]
*No. I have Song-i.*

[P117]
Veins bulging in my neck, I shouted,

[P118]
“Marriage is incredibly important! You can’t just brush it aside like that! Love between a man and a woman! Pure feelings! Don’t I get any of that?”

[P119]
“No. You don’t.”

[P120]
“Why?! Why not?!”

[P121]
Wipeng looked me up and down as if I were an insect.

[P122]
“Is that something a man who’s been frequenting pleasure houses since he was sixteen should say? Did you scatter your conscience along with your silver nyang?”

[P123]
“……”

[P124]
“Let’s keep moving quietly. Our Lord is waiting.”

[P125]
If I’d actually been to one, at least I wouldn’t have felt so wronged.

[P126]
Fuck pleasure houses. I’d never even been to a pickup bar.

[P127]
As I kept silent and wept tears of blood inside, Chulwoo sidled over and asked,

[P128]
“Is that true?”

[P129]
“What is?”

[P130]
“That you’ve been visiting pleasure houses since you were sixteen.”

[P131]
“None of your business. Why are you suddenly asking?”

[P132]
Chulwoo flinched and began to ramble.

[P133]
“Well, how should I put it? Personal curiosity, perhaps. The curiosity of a man who has steadfastly walked only the path of a martial artist…”

[P134]
“You want to visit a pleasure house?”

[P135]
“Ahem!”

[P136]
“Stick to the path of a martial artist. Don’t wander down side roads.”

[P137]
I had barely finished answering with utter disdain when a voice cut in.

[P138]
“Young Hero Jin is absolutely right. How long has it been since you descended from the main sect? Have you already forgotten the duty of a martial artist?”

[P139]
The tone was stern, yet tinged with amusement.

[P140]
The unfamiliar voice belonged to a clean-cut man. He approached with steady steps and respectfully offered a fist-and-palm salute.

[P141]
But it wasn’t directed at me or Wipeng.

[P142]
“Baek Museong, First-generation Disciple of Huashan, pays his respects to his Martial Uncle.”

[P143]
Cheongpung remained silent for a moment before answering.

[P144]
“Who are you?”

[P145]
* * *

[P146]
He looked to be around sixty.

[P147]
The old man had a slender frame and strikingly narrow eyes.

[P148]
A deeply hoarse voice rasped through his chapped lips.

[P149]
“So you were utterly humiliated by some nameless nobody?”

[P150]
“E-Elder, that isn’t what happened…”

[P151]
The three men standing before him were sweating profusely.

[P152]
They were known as the Three Hands of Zhongnan, but in the presence of an elder of their sect, they had to watch every word and every movement.

[P153]
All the more so when that elder was the Roaring Fury Swordsman, a master counted among the five strongest in the Zhongnan Sect and a man notorious for his fiery temper.

[P154]
“Then what happened? No matter how I listen to this, all these old ears hear is that you bastards smeared shit all over the name of the great Zhongnan Sect.”

[P155]
The Three Hands of Zhongnan trembled beneath his piercing gaze.

[P156]
Just as the Roaring Fury Swordsman was about to unleash his wrath, one of the men, who had kept his mouth tightly shut the entire time, suddenly spoke.

[P157]
“He wasn’t a nameless nobody.”

[P158]
“What?”

[P159]
Gong Ilhyuk, the man with a splint on his arm, continued.

[P160]
“He said he was the Sword Saint’s Disciple.”

[P161]
The revelation was so shocking that the Roaring Fury Swordsman fell speechless. After a moment, he asked in disbelief,

[P162]
“…The Sword Saint?”

[P163]
“Yes.”

[P164]
“The Sword Saint, who has lived in seclusion all these years, raised a Disciple?”

[P165]
“We doubted him at first, but… it seems to be true.”

[P166]
“Your evidence?”

[P167]
“Li Feng, a lay Disciple of Huashan, serves in the military of Shanxi Province. Judging by his reaction, there can be little doubt.”

[P168]
“Li Feng?”

[P169]
The old man’s already wrinkled brow furrowed further.

[P170]
His memory wasn’t sharp enough to recall some lay Disciple of Huashan.

[P171]
“Is that all?”

[P172]
At the lukewarm response, Gong Ilhyuk hurriedly continued.

[P173]
“He has mastered Huashan’s supreme secret arts to the Peak level despite being barely twenty. He displayed one martial art after another that only the main sect’s direct Disciples are permitted to learn…”

[P174]
After hearing the full account of what had happened, the Roaring Fury Swordsman silently stroked his sword scabbard.

[P175]
*The Sword Saint’s Disciple. The Sword Saint’s Disciple.*

[P176]
The Sword Saint had been in seclusion for decades.

[P177]
No one even knew whether he was alive or dead, yet now his Disciple had suddenly appeared in Murim?

[P178]
It was hard to believe, but the Roaring Fury Swordsman was already inclined to accept it.

[P179]
*At the very least, I should confirm it for myself.*

[P180]
After a long silence, the Roaring Fury Swordsman abruptly rose from his seat and issued an order to the startled Three Hands of Zhongnan.

[P181]
“Guide me.”

[P182]
“W-Where?”

[P183]
“Do you mean to the Sword Saint’s Disciple…?”

[P184]
Unlike the other two, who stood there flustered, Gong Ilhyuk’s eyes flashed.

[P185]
“As far as I know, he is traveling with a scion of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P186]
“A scion of the Jin Family of Taiyuan? You mean that Jin Taekyung fellow you mentioned earlier?”

[P187]
“Yes. He’s half a day’s journey from here.”

[P188]
The Roaring Fury Swordsman clicked his tongue.

[P189]
“You cunning bastard. That’s why you came looking for this old man, isn’t it?”

[P190]
“The name of the great Zhongnan Sect has been dragged through the dirt because of your inept Disciples. Elder, no one cares more deeply for our sect than you. I happened to hear that you were nearby on business, so…”

[P191]
“Enough. From what you’ve told me, that Jin Taekyung fellow sounds extraordinarily arrogant as well.”

[P192]
“That’s right. A bastard like him needs to be taught a harsh lesson.”

[P193]
As if the thought had only just occurred to him, Gong Ilhyuk added,

[P194]
“I hear the Jin Family of Taiyuan is holding a gathering.”

[P195]
“A gathering?”

[P196]
“They invited every sect in Shanxi Province so they could flaunt their power.”

[P197]
“They trampled on our sect, and now they’re holding a gathering?”

[P198]
Anger flared in the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s eyes.

[P199]
“I’ve heard enough. Lead the way.”

[P200]
“I obey, Elder.”

[P201]
A triumphant smile spread across Gong Ilhyuk’s lips.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.

- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
